text:
incident-bot: Pager: high p95 token latency for inference API in AZ us-east-1a. Error spike: DNS timeouts + increased socket retransmits. PagerID: INC-2026-0421.
maya: i’m on it, joining. seeing elevated grpc stream retries and partial responses (stream cut).
raj: +1 oncall. are we seeing model-load failures or network-level?
leo: looks networky — host rx errors and some ENI attach logs around 03:12Z. DNS resolver latency jumped to ~700ms p95.
maya: kv-cache churn observed, lots of kvcache misses causing model warmups -> extra latency.
nick_ops: moving traffic away from us-east-1a to us-east-1b + eu-west-1 for critical routes. starting gradual reroute now.
maya: do we have a runbook step for DNS resolver backoff?
sre-robot: runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/az-dns-evac. Steps: 1) increase resolver retries, 2) steer gold-tier traffic, 3) enable model-fallback policy.
leo: executed traffic steer via router flag: `traffic.reroute.region=us-east-1b` (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
abigail: CS: prepping customer comms. which customers affected? some dedicated & hosted tenants seeing streaming truncation.
maya: affected: hosted API p95 > 5s for a subset; Dedicated nodes in that AZ seeing degraded qps. Not all customers, mostly streaming endpoints and long-context requests.
nick_ops: temporarily disabled cross-AZ affinity for ephemeral hosts in that AZ to allow faster redispatch.
raj: let's enable model fallback to smaller quantized variants for streaming endpoints to keep tails bounded. maya please coordinate.
maya: enabling fallback: policy `fallback=redwood-v1-quantized-small` for streaming routes. Applying now.
incident-bot: Action: model-fallback policy applied to route /v1/stream (canary 25%).
leo: dns resolver thundering observed on local cache refresh. Increasing resolver cache TTL from 30s -> 300s as emergency measure.
nick_ops: also toggled connection-retry thresholds: grpc.keepalive_time reduced to 10s to surface failures faster.
abigail: drafting message for customers: short outage note + mitigation steps. Will flag impacted tenants and offer dedicated support.
support-bot: Logged ticket for impacted hosted customers and bumped severity to P1 for those with streaming SLAs.
maya: monitoring p50/p95 now. p50 improved after reroute, p95 still elevated on some streams (kvcache regen).
leo: observed one noisy host with NIC retransmit flood -> cordon and drain initiated for that instance.
raj: good, keep draining noisy hosts. what's the ETA for full switchover to us-east-1b?
nick_ops: switchover ETA ~ 12m to reach 100% for critical routes; non-critical by 30m.
maya: rolling canary of fallback model to 50% reduced tail latency by ~1.8s. continuing.
abigail: sending customers initial note now, include link to status page and offer webhook for event updates.
incident-bot: customer-impact summary: partial streaming degradation for ~6 hosted tenants and 2 dedicated pools in us-east-1a. No data loss. Mitigations: traffic reroute, model fallback, host drains, resolver TTL increase.
sre-robot: recommend post-incident: investigate resolver bucket rate limiting in that AZ and evaluate health checks for ENI early detection.
raj: agreed. maya & leo take action items. abigail to handle follow-ups and template. i'll start incident timeline doc.
maya: will update when p95 < 500ms for all routes.
leo: pulling NIC counters and ENI attach logs, will dump to incident artifacts.
abigail: CS: queued prioritized outreach for impacted enterprise customers.
incident-bot: On-call handoff scheduled in 2 hours unless resolved.
maya: logging final mitigation steps in runbook. continuing monitoring, will @channel when moved to postmortem.
